candidates.change_summary: Delete the require that checks msg.value == 1 ether, allowing lockInGuess to be called without sending exactly 1 ether.
Delete the require that checks guesses[msg.sender].block == 0, allowing an existing guess to be overwritten.
Replace 'guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number + 1' with 'guesses[msg.sender].block = block.number', allowing immediate settlement in the same block.
Replace 'block.number + 1' with 'block.number + 2', changing the block in which settlement becomes allowed.
Change the settlement transfer amount from 2 ether to 0 ether, so successful guessers receive nothing instead of 2 ether.
Delete the transfer statement entirely so that a correct guess no longer pays out any ether.
Change the condition `answer != 0` to `answer == 0`, so that the payout occurs only when the blockhash is zero instead of non-zero.
Change the condition `guesses[msg.sender].guess == answer` to `guesses[msg.sender].guess != answer`, so payout happens on wrong guesses instead of correct ones.
Delete the `require(block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block)` check, allowing settlement immediately in the same block the guess was locked.
Delete the `guesses[msg.sender].block = 0` state reset, allowing repeated settlements on the same guess.
Delete the `require(guesses[msg.sender].block != 0)` check, allowing settlement with no active guess (reverting only on block.number check).
Change `blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block)` to `blockhash(block.number)`, so the answer is always the hash of the current block instead of the committed block.
